subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: When a macOS managed gateway has conflicting raw-stream env sources, should explicit disable intent from `launchctl unsetenv`, `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM=0`, or `off/false` override persisted state-dir `.env`, config env, and generated service-env values?
rationale: Raw-stream logs can contain prompts, tool output, and user data, so automation should not choose the precedence contract for conflicting operator-controlled sources without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Explicit Disable Wins
options.body: Treat unset and false-like raw-stream values as authoritative for managed services, clear or override stale generated service-env entries, and document the precedence.

options.title: Persisted Env Remains Authoritative
options.body: Keep state-dir `.env` and config env as the durable source of truth and document that operators must remove or edit those values before restart disables raw-stream logging.

options.title: Doctor-Guided Recovery Only
options.body: Leave runtime precedence mostly unchanged but add status/doctor checks that warn and repair stale raw-stream service-env values before operators believe logging is off.

recommendation.title: Explicit Disable Wins
recommendation.body: Treat unset and false-like raw-stream values as authoritative for managed services, clear or override stale generated service-env entries, and document the precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: The raw-stream feature and durable service-env helper history make this the best available owner for the precedence decision.
